Triangle-free bases satisfy pointed-complex Proposition 4.3 on n+m vertices with m circuits, hence S^(n-1). Natural edge-facet nerve identification and equivariant Alexander duality yield sign(V+E)*sign(E)=sign(V) over Z. Exceptional m=1 checked directly; finite mod-two homology and fourteen integer Lefschetz checks corroborate.

value.rationale: An all-graph, nontrivial simple-homotopy dichotomy detects a base triangle using the topology of a natural three-clique-free construction even though the starting complex has no cone apex. It identifies exactly where the known pointed sphere disappears. The new integral automorphism sign module is uniform, depends only on original-vertex parity, and cannot be inferred merely from Betti numbers. It gives a reusable equivariant test beyond the older non-equivariant result; no arbitrary finite slice is chosen.
